subject: Nimbus implementation: cost & latency tuning — quantization + routing checkpoints
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Charlie Ramos <charlie.r@nimbus.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus implementation: initial cost/latency tuning notes

Charlie / Priya —

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Per our convo, I wanted to capture a short, pragmatic plan for the first two weeks of implementation focused on cost / performance trade-offs we expect to tune during onboarding. Monica (CS lead) is looped to own day-to-day execution.

Summary (two-week priority):
- Target SLOs: 99th pct tail <= 350ms for short-chat flows (<=128 tokens), average cost per 1k tokens target $X (we'll confirm after initial profiling).
- Quick knobs to iterate: batching policy (max batch latency 40ms / batch size goal ~8–16), prefix/KV caching for stable prompt prefixes, quantization profile candidates (int8 dynamic vs awq-6 small-accuracy loss profile), and routing policy (primary model + fallback cheaper variant for non-critical requests).

Ask from Nimbus before Monday: a sample traffic trace (anonymized) showing request size distribution and % of repeated prefixes (can be a CSV or simple histogram). That will let us pick a default quant profile and a baseline batcher config.

I attached a short checklist and a draft quant profile CSV for us to iterate on. Proposed next steps:
1) Monica to run a 2-day profiling job on your staging traffic (we'll provide a small test harness).
2) Align on cost target and confirm any hard latency ceilings per route.
3) Apply conservative quant profile on a canary path and measure quality delta on your evaluation prompts.

Monica — can you take point on the profiling run? Monica / Charlie — propose a 30m call Wednesday to align on the data handoff and test windows.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Charlie Ramos <charlie.r@nimbus.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-08T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus implementation: initial cost/latency tuning notes

Thanks Karthik — happy to take lead.

Charlie / Priya — quick clarifications so we scope profiling correctly:
- Is staging traffic representative of peak weekend load? If not, please indicate expected peak RPS and a 'typical' workday RPS.
- We'll need a sample of 1k requests with the original prompt + model variant indicated (if available). A CSV with columns: request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, repeated_prefix_label (yes/no) is ideal.

Plan on our side:
- Day 0–1: deploy small probe harness (Karthik's sample harness) to run 1k requests against the current model and the two quant candidates in our internal test env.
- Day 2–3: collect latency/cost/quality metrics and surface a recommended default config (batching, cache TTLs, quant profile).

Can we schedule the sync Wednesday 2028-06-09 at 10:00am PT? If yes I'll share a calendar invite and the profiling instructions.

Attachments: implementation-checklist.pdf (checklist), sample-routing-config.yaml (routing polite fallback example).

Monica

--
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

From: Charlie Ramos <charlie.r@nimbus.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2028-06-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus implementation: initial cost/latency tuning notes

Sounds good — Wednesday at 10:00am PT works. Quick context that should inform the tuning:
- Peak RPS (prod): ~45 RPS; staging is ~15 RPS peak. We can run the profiling on a scaled-staging instance that mimics 30 RPS if needed.
- Latency SLO: For UI chat flows we need 95th <= 300ms; we can tolerate up to 450ms at the 99th for long generation paths but cost is a hard constraint — we'd like to keep avg inference cost below $0.60 / 1k tokens on average.
- Prefix reuse: ~42% of requests include repeated system/user framing that benefits from KV caching.

I'll drop a 1k-row CSV into the Drive link and grant your team access by EOD. Also, we are comfortable trying an int8 profile if quality on our eval set stays within a 1.5% delta in F1/relevance.

Charlie

--
Charlie Ramos
Head of Product, Nimbus.ai
charlie.r@nimbus.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Nimbus implementation: initial cost/latency tuning notes

On Fri, Jun 9, 2028 at 10:15 AM Charlie Ramos <charlie.r@nimbus.ai> wrote:
> Sounds good — Wednesday at 10:00am PT works. Quick context that should inform the tuning:
> - Peak RPS (prod): ~45 RPS; staging is ~15 RPS peak. We can run the profiling on a scaled-staging instance that mimics 30 RPS if needed.
> - Latency SLO: For UI chat flows we need 95th <= 300ms; we can tolerate up to 450ms at the 99th for long generation paths but cost is a hard constraint — we'd like to keep avg inference cost below $0.60 / 1k tokens on average.
> - Prefix reuse: ~42% of requests include repeated system/user framing that benefits from KV caching.

Thanks for the context — helpful. A couple quick operational notes before tomorrow's sync:
- Monica will run the 2-day profiling window on your scaled staging (30 RPS) starting Monday morning; she'll share the harness and a Docker image for the probe.
- Our recommended default to test Canary 1 is: int8 dynamic quant + cache enabled with a 5-minute TTL for repeated prefixes + batching target window 30ms (max batch 16). That should reduce units by ~28–35% in our estimate while keeping quality within your stated 1.5% delta on typical prompts — we'll validate.
- Fallback routing: primary model for low-latency UI flows; cheaper quant variant (same architecture + int8 aggressive) for background/async jobs. We'll produce a sample routing config (attached).

Marissa — tagging you because we may need a one-off capacity reserve if Nimbus wants to spike beyond the Dedicated commitment in the first 72 hours. Can you approve a 48-hour burst pool from the shared warm capacity if the canary indicates it's needed?

Thanks — see you on the sync.
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Final note for the runbook: please ensure all canary runs log token-level billing breakdowns and we tag those metrics with "nimbus_onboard_canary_v1" so finance can back out the surge.

Marissa
